title: The William Morris deal and the confusion at the Oriental Theater in Chicago
summary: Taking a pay cut from $750 to $350, they get a Chicago contract, but the stage doorman sends them to the wrong theatre first.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So I go to the William Morris office whom I knew and who knew us and offered them an act with a cut of $350, cut the salary from $750 to $350, understand? To go on any date to Chicago. They're going to give us transportation to Chicago, a couple hundred dollars cash plus the contract to work at the

Orpheum Theater -- no, the Oriental Theater in Chicago with Paul Ash who was The Blue Streak of Vaudeville, another blue streak, he was the King Leader of Bands at that time -- Paul Ash. And we got there for the rehearsal, when we come to the stage door, the stage door man could not believe that we had come there to work. So he calls upstairs to tell them we were downstairs at the door to come to work. When the man come down to see us, he said we got the wrong place -- got the wrong place, I got the contract in my pocket for the Oriental Theater -- look at that one, look at this one. I got the contract in my pocket for the Oriental Theater in Chicago, Illinois, the date to start and all and I'm here at the theater. And the man don't want to receive me because I'm in the wrong place. I said, yeah? He said, "Wait a minute." So he goes back upstairs, gets on the phone and calls up another theater where we had played, all the four of us Nazarro, Buck and Bubbles had played on the west

side of town to tell them about us and ask for a date for us, and got a date for us. Come back and says, you got the wrong theater, the theater is the west side theater, I think he said the Ordean Theater over on the west side. Okay. So they expect you there. That's okay. I go to the theater, rehearse, go on do the show, the same guy that produces the show that Paul Ash is in, he went to see the show, too. He went to catch the show. When he caught the show, he came back to the theater and we got the message that they wanted us over with Paul Ash the following week. Okay. When we come to open the following week, the piana had to be changed from where it was where we saw it, they weren't using it for years, it was on my left of the stage -- on my left, the piano was over here, understand?
